title: Transfer Learning for Dislocation Defect Quantification
content: Quantifying the impact of irradiation on a material in a micrograph involves identifying and localizing dislocation defects such as loops and lines. This has typically been done by an instrument scientist and aided with an image analysis tool like ImageJ. But this type of analysis is not only time-intensive but also difficult to reproduce and produces results that can be highly subjective, especially in noisy micrographs. Advances in machine learning computer vision models offer the prospect of automated dislocation defect quantification that is both reproducible and fast. However, computer vision models are generally trained on tens of thousands of annotated images whereas there are not nearly so many annotated micrographs of irradiated materials with dislocation defects available. Recognizing this lack of annotated training data for micrographs, several researchers have built custom machine learning models and produced high quality identification and localizations on dislocation defects for low noise micrographs but did not release the source code of the models nor examine high noise micrographs. But more importantly, those efforts have not generally leveraged the widely used computer vision models built around transfer learning such as the You Only Look Once (YOLO) framework [1]. This work reports the results of using the recently released YOLO11 framework that heavily relies upon transfer learning to produce high quality dislocation defect annotations even when trained on small training dataset sizes. The resulting model and weights are released as open source and are available [2].
